metaDescription: Six cordless chainsaws compared on bar length, battery energy, chain speed and safety features, so you can pick one for storm cleanup, pruning or firewood.
expertTake: The EGO POWER+ CS1613 is the best cordless chainsaw in this group: a 16 inch bar, a brushless motor, tool-free tensioning and a 56V 4.0Ah battery in the box. The Seesii 40V 18-inch is the value pick because it ships with two 5.0Ah batteries, two chargers and a spare chain. If you cut more than a couple of cords of firewood a year or fell trees with trunks thicker than the bar, skip cordless and buy a gas saw.
introParagraphs: Battery chainsaws have gone from pruning toys to genuine firewood tools. For storm cleanup, limbing and cutting the occasional downed tree, a good cordless saw now starts instantly, runs quietly enough for a suburban street, and skips the carburetor headaches that sideline so many gas saws after a season in the shed.

Choosing one is mostly a question of matching bar length, battery platform and motor to the wood you actually cut. This guide explains those tradeoffs in plain terms, along with the safety and maintenance details that separate a dependable saw from a frustrating one. Our top picks are above, followed by detailed reviews of each model.

products.name: EGO POWER+ CS1613 16 inch 56V Cordless Chainsaw
products.description:
The CS1613 pairs a 16 inch bar with a brushless motor and a 56V 4.0Ah battery. Its chain is a 3/8 inch pitch, 0.043 inch gauge design with 56 drive links, which is the standard setup for a homeowner saw of this size and means replacement chains are easy to find. EGO compares it to a 40cc gas saw, which is a marketing label, but 16 inches of bar is genuinely the sweet spot for limbing, storm cleanup and small firewood rounds.

Battery energy is where it beats the smaller EGO CS1201. The 4.0Ah pack stores about 224 watt-hours (56V times 4.0Ah), compared to roughly 140 watt-hours for the CS1201's 2.5Ah pack, so you get more cuts per charge and less sag under load. The listing makes slightly inconsistent cut-count claims, so treat them as approximate. It works with all EGO 56V ARC Lithium batteries, which is useful if you already own EGO mowers or blowers.

Ownership is easy. A tool-free dial adjusts chain tension, an IPX4 rating protects against splashing, and the low-profile design lets you cut flush to the ground. Keep the bar oil reservoir topped up, because a dry chain overheats the bar and drains the battery. Sharpen or replace the chain when it makes dust instead of chips. Compared with the Greenworks 80V 18 inch, you give up two inches of bar but get a simpler, lighter saw and a battery platform with a broad tool lineup.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want a balanced 16 inch saw for storm cleanup, limbing and small firewood.
pros: Brushless motor with a large 4.0Ah battery included
Tool-free tensioning dial makes chain adjustments simple
IPX4 rating tolerates damp conditions and splashes
Works with the whole EGO 56V battery family
cons: Cut-per-charge claims in the listing are inconsistent with each other
16 inch bar limits felling capacity for larger trees
Gas-equivalent claim is marketing, not a measurement

products.name: Greenworks 80V 16 inch Brushless Cordless Chainsaw
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V 16 inch uses a brushless motor with a quoted 25 m/s chain speed, faster than the EGO CS1613's 20 m/s. Chain speed matters because a faster chain slices wood fibers cleanly instead of tearing them, provided the motor has the torque to hold the speed under load. Greenworks says it delivers the equivalent of a 50cc gas saw, which is an optimistic marketing comparison.

It lists a mechanical chain brake for kickback safety, an automatic oiler and side-access tensioning. The side-access design means you adjust chain tension from the side cover, which is more of a hassle than a tool-free dial but keeps the chain secure. The battery is 80V at 2.5Ah, about 200 watt-hours by the simple volts-times-Ah math, or less than the 4.0Ah EGO pack at 224. Note that 80V is a maximum-voltage label, so compare the energy figure and not just the headline voltage.

In use, this saw is aimed at homeowners who need to tackle yard projects and storm cleanup. It is more powerful than the EGO CS1201 and similar to the CS1613, with a better listed brake. The battery platform is a key consideration: Greenworks says the 80V line shares batteries across a large range of tools, so buying into it works well if you want a mower, trimmer and blower on one pack. Keep the oiler reservoir filled and the chain sharp.
products.bestFor: Storm cleanup and yard work where a chain brake and fast chain speed matter.
pros: Listed 25 m/s chain speed is faster than the EGO saws
Mechanical chain brake for added kickback protection
Brushless motor with automatic chain oiler
80V battery platform shares with other Greenworks tools
cons: 2.5Ah battery holds less energy than the EGO 4.0Ah pack
Side-access tensioning is slower than a tool-free dial
Gas-equivalent claim is marketing, not a measurement

products.name: Greenworks 80V 18 inch Brushless Cordless Chainsaw
products.description:
This 80V saw steps up to an 18 inch bar with a brushless motor and a 2.0Ah battery in the box. The 80V 2.0Ah pack stores about 160 watt-hours by volts times amp-hours, which is the smallest battery among the 80V and 56V saws here other than the EGO CS1201's 140 watt-hours. An 18 inch bar on a small battery is a mismatch: the saw can cut larger limbs, but the pack will drain faster than the 16 inch version with a 2.5Ah battery.

The listing claims up to 150 cuts on 4x4 lumber and the equivalent of a 42cc gas saw. Those are marketing claims, and the spec sheet gives no chain speed, so we cannot compare it directly with the 25 m/s Greenworks 16 inch. It includes an automatic oiler and easy-adjust tensioning for bar and chain maintenance, and push-button start with no gas or carburetor.

The practical advice is to buy a larger battery with this saw, which is easy given the 75-plus tool compatibility within the Greenworks 80V family. It is a good fit if you already own Greenworks 80V tools and want more bar for medium limbs. Otherwise, the Greenworks 16 inch with its listed chain brake is the better-documented option, and the EGO CS1613 offers more battery capacity.
products.bestFor: Existing Greenworks 80V owners who want extra bar length for medium limbs.
pros: 18 inch bar handles larger limbs than the 16 inch saws
Brushless motor with automatic oiler reduces upkeep
Shares batteries with 75 plus Greenworks 80V tools
Push-button start with no gas, spark plug or carburetor
cons: Small 2.0Ah battery drains quickly on an 18 inch bar
Listing gives no chain speed or brake information
42cc gas equivalent is marketing, not a measurement

products.name: Seesii 40V 18 inch Brushless Cordless Chainsaw Kit
products.description:
The Seesii is a kit-first saw: an 18 inch bar, a 2200W brushless motor, two 40V 5.0Ah batteries, two chargers and two chains. Two 5.0Ah packs store about 400 watt-hours combined by volts times Ah, nearly double the single 224 watt-hour pack in the EGO CS1613, so it can run through a heavy afternoon of cuts when you swap batteries. For occasional users, that is a better start than any single-battery kit here.

The chain speed is listed at 30 ft/s, which converts to about 9 m/s. That is far slower than the EGO saws at up to 20 m/s and the Greenworks 16 inch at 25 m/s. A slower chain cuts less aggressively, so the saw leans on its big bar and battery rather than speed. The weight is listed as 8.6 lb with both batteries, which is odd because a saw cannot take two packs at once, so confirm the weight with a single pack installed.

It lists a rapid emergency brake, an enlarged hand guard, a dual-action safety switch, an 80 ml automatic oiler and tool-less tensioning. The listing notes some initial installation is required, so expect to mount the bar and chain yourself. Seesii is a lesser-known brand, so check replacement-chain and battery availability and the support terms before you commit. It suits a budget-minded homeowner who wants maximum runtime without buying into a major battery platform.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want two batteries and a spare chain in a single box.
pros: Two 5.0Ah batteries store about 400 watt-hours combined
Includes two chargers and two chains for extra uptime
Emergency brake and dual-action switch listed as safety gear
Tool-less tensioning and an 80 ml automatic oiler
cons: Listed 30 ft/s chain speed is far slower than the EGO saws
Lesser-known brand, so parts and support are a question
Weight figure in the listing is ambiguous about one or two packs

products.name: EGO POWER+ CS1201 12 inch 56V Cordless Chainsaw
products.description:
The CS1201 is the compact EGO: a 12 inch bar, 45 drive link chain, brushless motor and a 56V 2.5Ah battery, weighing just 8.4 lb with the pack attached. Light weight matters more than most buyers realize because chainsaw fatigue ruins accuracy and raises accident risk. EGO compares it to a 30cc gas saw, and the claim is more modest and more believable for a 12 inch bar than the 40cc claim on the CS1613.

It is designed for light-duty brush removal and limb work. The chain shares the same 3/8 inch pitch and 0.043 gauge as the CS1613, but with 45 links instead of 56, and the 2.5Ah battery stores roughly 140 watt-hours against 224 on the CS1613. The listing quotes up to 130 cuts on a 4x4 with this pack, an optimistic number you should treat as best case. It works with 56V ARC batteries 5.0Ah and lower, so a bigger pack is a straightforward upgrade.

Tool-free tensioning keeps field adjustments quick, and for pruning from a ladder or tackling small branches, the weight advantage is real. It is not the saw for firewood or felling. If you may cut anything over 8 inches thick, spend the extra for the CS1613 or a longer-bar saw. Store the battery indoors at moderate temperature and keep chain oil in the reservoir.
products.bestFor: Light pruning, brush cleanup and anyone who values low weight over bar length.
pros: Weighs only 8.4 lb with the battery attached, easy on the arms
Brushless motor with tool-free chain tensioning for quick fixes
Compatible with larger EGO 56V batteries up to 5.0Ah
Compact 12 inch bar is easy to control on small limbs
cons: 12 inch bar limits it to light-duty cutting jobs and pruning
Cut-count claim is a best-case figure taken from the listing

products.name: DeWalt FLEXVOLT 60V 16 inch Cordless Chainsaw with 2Ah Battery
products.description:
The listing for this DeWalt gives only a name: FLEXVOLT 60V, 2Ah battery, 16 inch bar. No chain speed, motor type, brake or runtime data is provided, so everything beyond those three facts is general knowledge, not model-specific data. FLEXVOLT is DeWalt's battery system that switches between 20V and 60V tools, and a 60V max label is a peak voltage, not the nominal figure.

The bar length matches the EGO CS1613 and the Greenworks 80V 16 inch, so cutting capacity should be similar. The 2Ah pack, however, is the smallest in the roundup, so we expect it to drain faster than the 4.0Ah EGO pack or either of the Seesii 5.0Ah batteries. Many FLEXVOLT owners buy bigger packs for this reason, and that is the intended path for a DeWalt user who already owns the batteries.

This saw makes sense mainly for people already invested in the DeWalt 20V and 60V battery ecosystem, because sharing packs across tools saves money. If you are starting from scratch, the EGO CS1613 comes with a larger battery and clearer published specs. Check whether the listing includes a charger, as the title does not mention one. Keep the chain sharp and the oil topped up as with any cordless saw.
products.bestFor: Buyers already invested in the DeWalt 20V and FLEXVOLT battery ecosystem.
pros: Runs on the DeWalt FLEXVOLT 60V platform for pack sharing
16 inch bar gives the same reach as the EGO CS1613
Brand has a deep service and battery accessory network
Larger FLEXVOLT packs can be added when you need runtime
cons: Listing gives no chain speed, brake or motor details
Included 2Ah battery is the smallest in this roundup
Not clear whether a charger is included from the title

buyingCriteria.explanation: The bar sets the maximum cut diameter, though the effective cut is a couple of inches less than the bar length because the chain wraps the nose. A 12 inch bar like the EGO CS1201 suits branches up to roughly 8 inches, a 16 inch bar like the CS1613 handles most homeowner work, and an 18 inch bar like the Seesii or Greenworks 80V is for larger limbs. A common mistake is buying the longest bar available. A longer bar needs more motor torque and battery energy, so on small packs it simply empties them faster.

Watt-hours (volts times amp-hours) tell you how much work a pack can do. The EGO CS1613 pack stores about 224 Wh, the Greenworks 80V 2.5Ah about 200 Wh, the Greenworks 18 inch about 160 Wh, the EGO CS1201 about 140 Wh, and the Seesii packs about 200 Wh each. Voltage labels like 80V or 60V are often maximum figures, so they do not compare cleanly across brands. Always buy at least one spare battery if you plan to cut for more than 20 minutes at a stretch.

Chain speed determines how cleanly the saw slices wood fibers. EGO quotes up to 20 m/s, Greenworks 25 m/s, and Seesii 30 ft/s, which is only about 9 m/s. Brushless motors waste less energy as heat and deliver more torque per watt-hour, which is why all these saws use them. Be careful with gas-equivalent claims such as 30cc on the CS1201 or 50cc on the Greenworks 16 inch, because there is no standard test behind them.

Kickback is the main chainsaw injury risk, and a chain brake stops the chain in a fraction of a second when the front guard is pushed forward. The Greenworks 16 inch lists a mechanical chain brake, and Seesii lists an emergency brake plus a dual-action switch. The EGO listings do not mention a brake in the bullets, though many saws include one. Check for a front hand guard, a trigger lock and an anti-kickback chain, and wear eye, ear and leg protection regardless of the saw.

A chain that is too loose can derail, and one that is too tight overheats the bar and bleeds battery. Tool-free tensioning, as on the EGO CS1613, CS1201 and Seesii, lets you adjust in the field. Greenworks uses side-access tensioning. An automatic oiler keeps the bar lubricated, but you must keep the reservoir full: the Seesii holds 80 ml. Check chain tension after the first few cuts on a new chain, as new chains stretch.

A chainsaw is rarely your only cordless tool, so the battery platform matters. EGO 56V, Greenworks 80V (75-plus compatible tools) and DeWalt FLEXVOLT all share packs across mowers, trimmers and blowers. Buying a saw on a platform you already own can save the cost of a battery and charger. Seesii is an unfamiliar platform with no broader tool lineup, so its two included batteries are the main reason to pick it.

specDecoder.meaning: The length of the guide bar the chain runs around. The usable cutting length is shorter by roughly the nose radius, so a 16 inch bar cuts about 14 inches.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not pair a long bar with a small battery. The Greenworks 18 inch comes with a 2.0Ah pack.

specDecoder.meaning: Voltage is electrical pressure and amp-hours is capacity. Multiply them to get watt-hours, the real measure of how much energy the pack stores.
specDecoder.watchFor: 80V and 60V labels are often maximum figures. The EGO 56V 4.0Ah pack stores more energy than the Greenworks 80V 2.0Ah.

specDecoder.meaning: How fast the chain travels around the bar, measured in meters per second or feet per second. Faster chains cut cleaner if the motor can hold speed under load.
specDecoder.watchFor: Units differ across listings. 20 m/s is about 66 ft/s, so the Seesii's 30 ft/s is much slower.

specDecoder.meaning: A marketing comparison to the displacement of a gasoline engine, such as 30cc on the CS1201 or 40cc on the CS1613. It describes rough class, not measured output.
specDecoder.watchFor: No standard test exists. Use bar length, battery energy and chain speed instead.

specDecoder.meaning: The number of cuts through a test piece, usually a 4x4, on one battery. It is a rough runtime indicator that depends on wood species and chain sharpness.
specDecoder.watchFor: Claims vary: the EGO CS1613 listing quotes both 130 and 220. Treat them as best-case figures.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared bar lengths (12, 16 and 18 inches), chain specifications and listed cut-per-charge claims. The 12 inch EGO CS1201 sits at the small end, while the 18 inch Greenworks and Seesii saws sit at the top. We discounted cut-count claims because they come from the manufacturers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery energy
howWeEvaluated.description: We converted each battery to watt-hours by multiplying volts and amp-hours. The Seesii kit (two 5.0Ah packs) leads in total energy, followed by the EGO CS1613 at about 224 Wh per pack. The DeWalt 2Ah pack and Greenworks 18 inch 2.0Ah pack trail.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for chain brakes, hand guards, trigger locks and weather resistance. The Greenworks 16 inch lists a mechanical brake, Seesii lists an emergency brake and dual-action switch, and the EGO CS1613 lists IPX4 weather resistance. Listings with no safety data were marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Maintenance design
howWeEvaluated.description: We assessed tensioning and oiling: tool-free dials on the EGO saws and Seesii, side access on Greenworks, and automatic oilers on the Greenworks and Seesii models. These features determine how often you reach for a wrench or an oil can.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform and documentation
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how deep each battery platform is (EGO 56V, Greenworks 80V with 75-plus tools, DeWalt FLEXVOLT) and how complete the spec data is. The DeWalt listing offered almost no model-specific detail, which limited its ranking.

cards.label: Short bar (12 to 16 inches)
cards.text: Less chain to drive means lower current draw, less weight and better battery life. The EGO CS1201 (12 inch), EGO CS1613 (16 inch), Greenworks 80V 16 inch and DeWalt FLEXVOLT 16 inch belong here. They suit pruning, limbing and rounds up to roughly 10 to 12 inches.

cards.label: Long bar (18 inches)
cards.text: More cutting capacity per pass, but more drag, so the pack drains faster and a bigger battery is essential. The Seesii 40V and the Greenworks 80V 18 inch fall here. The Seesii compensates with two 5.0Ah batteries, while the Greenworks ships with a 2.0Ah pack.

howToChoose.note: Pick a short bar if you mainly prune and limb. Pick the Seesii if you need the 18 inch capacity and want enough battery to use it.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A sharp chain, a bar of at least 16 inches, plenty of battery energy and a spare pack. Firewood bucking means many consecutive cuts, which drains small packs. Cordless saws suit up to about a cord a year; beyond that, a gas saw is better value.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Seesii 40V 18 inch is the best firewood pick because of its two 5.0Ah batteries, while the EGO POWER+ CS1613 is the best single-battery option with 224 Wh in the pack. The EGO CS1201 and the DeWalt 2Ah kit are too small.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a mature battery platform, documented safety features and strong chain speed. The EGO CS1613 and Greenworks 80V 16 inch deliver those and justify a higher entry cost over the Seesii.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only cut a few times a year or want a spare battery included. The Seesii kit gives the most batteries per kit, and the EGO CS1201 gives you a lightweight saw for pruning.

maintenance.interval: When it makes dust instead of chips
maintenance.why: A dull chain forces the saw to push harder, which drains the battery and raises kickback risk. File the cutters evenly or have the chain sharpened.
Lack of lubrication overheats the bar and chain and burns battery capacity. Check the oil level with each battery swap.

maintenance.interval: After the first few cuts and every session
maintenance.why: New chains stretch quickly, and a loose chain can derail. Tension should allow the chain to pull snugly against the bar without binding.

maintenance.task: Clean the bar groove and oil port
maintenance.why: Sawdust packs the groove and blocks oil flow to the chain. Clearing it extends bar and chain life.
Lithium-ion packs last longer when stored indoors at partial charge, away from freezing or hot garages. Avoid leaving them fully drained.

maintenance.task: Inspect the chain brake and guard
maintenance.why: Sawdust and oil can stick the brake lever. Test it with the battery removed so you know it engages freely.

faq.q: Can a cordless chainsaw replace a gas chainsaw?
faq.a: For homeowners cutting under a couple of cords of firewood a year and doing storm cleanup, yes. Battery saws start instantly, make no fumes and need almost no tune-ups. For heavy forestry or daily professional use, gas still wins on endurance and raw power. Gas-equivalent claims like 40cc on the EGO CS1613 are marketing comparisons.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a cordless chainsaw?
faq.a: Think of it as a kit price. The Seesii includes two batteries and two chargers, making it the best value, while the EGO CS1613 and Greenworks 80V 16 inch cost more but offer better documented platforms. A saw that comes with only a 2.0Ah or 2Ah battery may require buying a second pack, which raises the true cost.

faq.q: How long do cordless chainsaw batteries last?
faq.a: Runtime depends on watt-hours, bar length and wood hardness. A 4.0Ah 56V pack stores about 224 Wh, and manufacturers claim around 130 cuts on a 4x4. Expect fewer in hardwood or with a dull chain. Lithium packs age with charge cycles and heat, typically giving several years of seasonal use if stored properly.

faq.q: Does a higher voltage mean a more powerful saw?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Voltage is only one part of power, and labels like 80V or 60V are often maximum voltages. Compare watt-hours, motor type and chain speed. The EGO 56V 4.0Ah pack stores more energy than the Greenworks 80V 2.0Ah pack, even though the Greenworks number looks bigger.

faq.q: What safety gear do I need with a cordless chainsaw?
faq.a: At minimum, eye protection, hearing protection, gloves, sturdy boots and cut-resistant chaps. A battery saw is quieter than gas, but it can still kick back. Use both hands, keep the bar below shoulder height and engage the chain brake when moving. Chain brakes are listed on the Greenworks 80V 16 inch and Seesii saws.

faq.q: What bar length do I need?
faq.a: Match the bar to the thickest wood you cut regularly, then add a couple of inches. A 12 inch bar like the EGO CS1201 suits branches, a 16 inch bar suits most yard work and small rounds, and an 18 inch bar is for larger limbs. Going longer than you need costs battery life and adds weight.
